Apart from providing in-house medical teams, PTCL also, throughout the year, sets-up special medical camps for under-privileged segments of society in rural areas as well as in educational institutes that cater to children with special needs. Earlier in 2016, one of the PTCL medical teams organized a 'Mega Mobile Medical Camp', which provided free screening of Hepatitis B and C, and vaccinations for Hepatitis B. The company also arranges free-of-cost medical checkups, offering free blood sugar and cholesterol testing, along with complimentary medicines for deserving patients and small gift hampers for children treated in the medical camps. PTCL commemorates and conducts focused activities on international days that draw the global spotlight on health issues such as diabetes, heart disease, hypertension and more. Health Awareness Sessions are also conducted through the year on major health issues such as infant and maternal mortality, and other topics. A total of 452 mobile medical units and health awareness activities were conducted in far flung areas in Pakistan, benefiting around 30,000 patients.

short_description: PROVIDING ACCESS TO QUALITY ECCD SERVICES FOR SYRIAN REFUGEE CHILDREN & GIRLS/BOYS FROM HOST COMMUNITIES IN JORDANTHE PROJECT?S OVERALL GOAL IS TO E
long_description: Providing Access to Quality ECCD Services for Syrian Refugee Children & Girls/Boys from host communities in JordanThe project?s overall goal is to ensure that boys and girls aged 5-6 from Syrian refugee and host communities in Jordan are adequately prepared for a successful transition to Grade 1 formal education. This program is working in alignment with the Jordanian Ministry of Education's renewed effort to improve quality and access to KG education. They aim to do this by increasing enrolment of children into KGs, supporting the expansion of KG classrooms, implementing teacher training programs, and enrolling out of school children into an accelerated learning program which will prepare them to enter the first grade. A supplemental aspect of this program is the implementation of the Educational Technology model that was developed as a result of the Humanitarian Accelerator hosted by Dubai Cares in 2017. This model will aim to support this program by using technology to support teacher training, learning at home, and parental engagement. This will act as a pilot for this model and the research conducted throughout the duration of the program will be used to further the discourse on how technology can be used to imporve education outcomes in general and education in emergencies in particular.-Increased access to safe, gender-sensitive KGs-Improved quality of learning environment at established KGs-Girls and boys without KG experience are prepared for a smooth transition to first grade through a 'School Readiness Program'-The aforementioned outcomes will all be supported through the piloting of an EdTech component that will support the teachers, students, and parents

long_description: WASH UP! Girl Talk educational programming sessions to increase their knowledge and practice of healthy hygiene behaviours and develop greater knowledge about the importance of adequate water and sanitation facilities for students especially girls. 4. Teachers will undergo multiple training sessions and will be provided with support to ensure that they have accurate information and out the program materials. 5.  Post-mortem meetings at the end of the implementation phase will allow for the collection of feedback from implementing teachers. This will inform modifications made during subsequent school terms. short_description: LITERACY ENHANCEMENT & NUTRITION SUPPORT (LENS)AS PART OF DUBAI CARES EFFORTS TO REACH THE MOST MARGINALIZED CHILDREN INCLUDING THOSE IN FAR REACHIN
long_description: Literacy Enhancement & Nutrition Support (LENS)As part of Dubai Cares efforts to reach the most marginalized children including those in far reaching places such as the Small Islands Developing States, Dubai Cares is supporting the school feeding program of the government of St. Vincent and the Grenadines as well as support the reading and learning of children in primary schools and the renovations of school kitchens.   Dubai Cares will support 12 schools with school feeding and reading assistance (benefitting 2,140 children) as well as support 10 schools with kitchen renovations (benefiting 2,819 children). The ZHTF is implementing a program targeted at assisting children in poor communities to attend school regularly. The program is comprised of several components: provision of school meals, books and other school supplies, medical examinations, including eye testing, and reading and learning assessments. In addition, the ZHTF executes a school feeding program in every primary school throughout the state to ensure that children receive adequate nutrition. The Ministry of Education manages this program with support from the Ministry of Health, Wellness and the Environment.

project_title: Providing Access to Quality ECCD Services for Syrian Refugee Children & Girls/Boys from host communities in JordanThe project?s overall goal is to ensure that boys and girls aged 5-6 from Syrian refugee and host communities in Jordan are adequately prepared for a successful transition to Grade 1 f
short_description: PROVIDING ACCESS TO QUALITY ECCD SERVICES FOR SYRIAN REFUGEE CHILDREN & GIRLS/BOYS FROM HOST COMMUNITIES IN JORDANTHE PROJECT?S OVERALL GOAL IS TO E
long_description: Providing Access to Quality ECCD Services for Syrian Refugee Children & Girls/Boys from host communities in JordanThe project?s overall goal is to ensure that boys and girls aged 5-6 from Syrian refugee and host communities in Jordan are adequately prepared for a successful transition to Grade 1 formal education. This program is working in alignment with the Jordanian Ministry of Education's renewed effort to improve quality and access to KG education. They aim to do this by increasing enrolment of children into KGs, supporting the expansion of KG classrooms, implementing teacher training programs, and enrolling out of school children into an accelerated learning program which will prepare them to enter the first grade. A supplemental aspect of this program is the implementation of the Educational Technology model that was developed as a result of the Humanitarian Accelerator hosted by Dubai Cares in 2017. This model will aim to support this program by using technology to support teacher training, learning at home, and parental engagement. This will act as a pilot for this model and the research conducted throughout the duration of the program will be used to further the discourse on how technology can be used to improve education outcomes in general and education in emergencies in particular.-Increased access to safe, gender-sensitive KGs-Improved quality of learning environment at established KGs-Girls and boys without KG experience are prepared for a smooth transition to first grade through a 'School Readiness Program'-The aforementioned outcomes will all be supported through the piloting of an EdTech component that will support the teachers, students, and parents

short_description: IMPROVING QUALITY OF EDUCATION THROUGH TRAINING OF SCHOOL LEADERS  THROUGH THE CREATING OF A LEADERSHIP ACADEMY IN INDONESIA, DUBAI CARES AND GLOBAL
long_description: Improving Quality of Education through training of School Leaders  Through the creating of a Leadership Academy in Indonesia, Dubai Cares and Global School Leaders aim to pilot a two-year on the job training program for school leaders serving in underperforming schools. Year 2: the program would consist of 1 day workshops conducted over five months and every other month in-school visits by the Leadership Academy program manager. The selection of the schools is focused on schools that cater to children in marginalized communities. Within the Indonesian context, the schools will be selected from the ?c Level? Accreditation schools, or the schools that are underperforming. For the pilot program, a diverse group of school leaders will be asked to participate in the program to test the model in multiple contexts.

long_description: Providing Access to Quality ECCD Services for Syrian Refugee Children & Girls/Boys from host communities in JordanThe project?s overall goal is to ensure that boys and girls aged 5-6 from Syrian refugee and host communities in Jordan are adequately prepared for a successful transition to Grade 1 formal education. This program is working in alignment with the Jordanian Ministry of Education's renewed effort to improve quality and access to KG education. They aim to do this by increasing enrolment of children into KGs, supporting the expansion of KG classrooms, implementing teacher training programs, and enrolling out of school children into an accelerated learning program which will prepare them to enter the first grade. A supplemental aspect of this program is the implementation of the Educational Technology model that was developed as a result of the Humanitarian Accelerator hosted by Dubai Cares in 2017. This model will aim to support this program by using technology to support teacher training, learning at home, and parental engagement. This will act as a pilot for this model and the research conducted throughout the duration of the program will be used to further the discourse on how technology can be used to imporve education outcomes in general and education in emergencies in particular.-Increased access to safe, gender-sensitive KGs-Improved quality of learning environment at established KGs-Girls and boys without KG experience are prepared for a smooth transition to first grade through a 'School Readiness Program'-The aforementioned outcomes will all be supported through the piloting of an EdTech component that will support the teachers, students, and parents

short_description: BUILDING A MOVEMENT OF TEACHER CHANGE MAKERS IN UGANDA AT THE HEART OF THE STIR APPROACH IS MEMBERSHIP OF LOCAL TEACHER CHANGE MAKER NETWORKS (ACTIV
long_description: Building a movement of Teacher change makers in Uganda At the heart of the STIR approach is membership of local teacher Change maker networks (active, regular communities of practice) that supports teachers in: 1. Developing teachers? mindsets and behaviours. 2. Building an enabling environment. 3. Pedagogical skills and knowledge. This takes place over a 2 year Teacher Development Journey as outlined below. Year 1: ?A buzz is created amongst teachers in their local area about the potential to be part of a STIR network, through in person discussions or formal communication channels. ?'Taster sessions' are run so teachers with a spark of innovation and commitment are identified, and invited to join the networks (typically of 30 to 40 teachers across 10 to 12 local schools). ?Teachers continue to integrate evidence-based approaches into their work, to understand the levers available to them to improve learning and know how to adapt these to their school context. In this way they can consistently improve the quality of teaching and learning, and become more effective practitioners over time. We focus on the key principles that make for an effective classroom and support teachers to adapt and implement these principles and to measure their impact through 3 learning improvement cycles. Year 2 Onwards: ?Leaders within each teacher network are identified and equipped with training and tools to sustain their local networks beyond the two year journey. An array of opportunities - from getting advanced training to influencing policy discussion - is made available to graduating teachers (Fellows) so they can go on to shape the movement at the local, regional, national and international levels. The clubs provide another experiential platform for students to acquire critical 21st Century and business/employability skills that will enable them to meet the demands of the labor market or create their own jobs if that market fails them. 3. Teacher Exchange Visits give teachers an opportunity to visit each other?s schools to see the innovative ways their peers are putting the new curriculum into practice. These visits encourage all teachers to adopt the competency-based pedagogical practices through accountability, learning, and coaching from their peers. 4. Educate! will also host a Student Business Competition.
